chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Usman, from Al-Halbi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
If he was of weak understanding, then say: 'O Allah, grant forgiveness to those who repented and followed Your way, and protect them from the punishment of the Hellfire.'
And when you do not know his state, then say: 'O Allah, if he loved goodness and its people, then forgive him, have mercy on him, and overlook him.'
And if the one of weak understanding is weaker than you in the Way (of Allah), then seek forgiveness for him based on the aspect of intercession, not based on the aspect of Wilayah.
ai.seo_question: What are the specific prayers for the deceased who had weak understanding or did not recognize Wilayah?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi outlines the nuanced practice of praying for the deceased who are considered 'weak in understanding' (ahl al-ghayl), distinguishing between supplicating for their forgiveness through intercession (shafa'ah) rather than by virtue of Wilayah. It provides specific du'as based on whether their spiritual state is known or unknown, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on mercy and the flexibility of prayer for those outside the full fold of religious authority. The distinction between praying 'on the face of intercession' versus 'on the face of Wilayah' highlights the theological boundary between general mercy and specific spiritual allegiance.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad Bin Usman, from Al Halby, 
from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘If he (the deceased) was of weak understanding, so say, ‘O Allahazwj! [40:7] Grant Forgiveness to those who repent and follow Your Way, and save them from the Punishment of the Blazing Fire’.

And when you do not know what his state is, so say, ‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! If he used to love the good and its people<sup>asws</sup>, so Forgive him, and be Merciful to him, and Overlook (his sins) from him;
and if he was of weaker understanding than yours in the Way (of Allahazwj), so seek Forgiveness for him upon the aspect of intercession, not upon the aspect of the Wilayah’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad ibn ‘Uthaman from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
If the deceased is a person of weak understanding, say, “O Lord, forgive those who have repented and followed Your path and protect them against suffering of the hell fire.”

If you do not know the condition of the deceased, then say, “O Lord, if this deceased is of those who love good and people of goodness, then forgive him, have mercy on him and ignore his shortcomings.”

If the deceased is a person of weak understanding, ask forgiveness for him in the form of intercession, not because of his right upon you as believing in Divine Authority of ’A’immah, Alayhim al-Salam.”’
